REQ-0001.text: The i2c_master_bit_ctrl module shall receive simple bit commands from the byte-level controller on the cmd input and translate each received command into timed SCL and SDA open-drain control sequences by driving scl_oen, sda_oen (with scl_o and sda_o as constant low drive values).
REQ-0001.reviewer: 0. Obligation test: the sentence says the module SHALL translate each received command into a timed scl_oen/sda_oen open-drain control sequence, with scl_o/sda_o constant low. A design that receives a supported command and never moves scl_oen/sda_oen from their released level, or that ever drives scl_o/sda_o non-zero, is condemned by these words -- this is a real obligation, not a definition or scope statement. 1. TRIGGER (per normalized.activation): ena=1, nReset=1, rst=0, i.e. a command may be processed, open until cmd_ack=1 or al=1. EFFECT: scl_o/sda_o stay 0 throughout the window; if the window closes via cmd_ack (a genuine completed sequence, since cmd_ack only pulses at the end of a real START/STOP/READ/WRITE sequence per impl. detail 10), at least one of scl_oen/sda_oen goes low somewhere in it. 2. CODE: applies = {ena:1,nReset:1,rst:0} (exactly normalized.activation.inputs, cmd not included), closes = cmd_ack:1 or al:1, windows = after(...,until=closes). For each window: throughout(scl_o==0 and sda_o==0); and, only when the window closed on cmd_ack==1, eventually(scl_oen==0 or sda_oen==0, strong). 3. False paths: (i) throughout fails on any row in the window where scl_o!=0

REQ-0006.text: The module detects arbitration loss and signals it by asserting al when the controller expects SDA to be high but the filtered SDA is observed low or when an unexpected STOP occurs during an active command.
REQ-0006.reviewer: Both open-conditions need the 'active command' qualifier rebuilt into the TRIGGER, not just the effect. Case 2 (_unexpected_stop) currently only excludes self-caused releases (edge in rose_sda_oen); it must additionally require that this controller currently has a command in progress, so an SDA rise-while-SCL-high produced by other bus traffic while this controller is idle does not open the window at all. Case 1 (_write_arbitration_check) currently treats din==1 & scl_i==1 & sda_i==0 as sufficient on its own; it must additionally require that a WRITE bit's stable-high/arbitration-check phase is actually underway, not merely that din happens to read 1 outside any command. As written, the oracle deliberately declined to gate on cmd (no fixed encoding available) but supplied no substitute observable proxy for 'active command', leaving both paths open on rows the requirement's 'during an active command' / expects-high-during-a-write language never covers -- deleting the assertion is not the fix, the window itself needs to be narrowed to command-active rows.

REQ-0066.text: The READ command sequence releases the SDA line so that the external slave can drive the data bit.
REQ-0066.reviewer: The unlicensed path is the eventually() False inside a window opened purely on cmd==4 & ena==1, with no confirmation that the FSM actually entered the READ sequence at that row -- cmd's value is only meaningful when sampled by an idle FSM, so a window can open (and close on an unrelated scl_oen fall) while a different command is still executing and sda_oen is legitimately 0 for that other command's own reasons. The TRIGGER needs to anchor window-open to the actual entry into the READ phase using observable ports available for this -- e.g. cmd==4 sampled specifically at the row following a cmd_ack pulse (or trace start/reset), which marks the FSM's idle decode point -- rather than any row where cmd merely happens to equal 4 while ena is high, regardless of what command is currently executing.

REQ-0093.text: When the core enable input ena is low, the module reloads the internal counter cnt from clk_cnt and normal command-FSM bit timing does not progress.

The check's TRIGGER (window-open condition, and ideally the window's continuation/close condition too) would need to become ena==0 AND nReset==1 AND rst==0 -- i.e. 'disabled and not in reset' -- so rows where reset is simultaneously active are excluded from the must-stay-stable claim, matching how the sibling checks in this spec gate on nReset/rst. Simply dropping the stability assertions is not the fix, since that would remove the genuine (non-reset) coverage this requirement calls for; the window needs to be rebuilt to exclude the reset-overlap case.

REQ-0020.text: The ena input is the core enable signal that gates normal timing and input filtering operation.
REQ-0020.reviewer: states_an_obligation is false: the sentence supplies neither a concrete trigger (it never says 'when ena is low/high', only labels ena as 'the core enable signal') nor a concrete effect (it never names a port or states what 'gates ... operation' looks like on any observable signal -- no hold, no suppressed pulse, nothing a trace could contradict). Both trigger and effect are missing in the sense that matters: the sentence describes ena's role/purpose rather than asserting an observable, violable behavior. Because there is no obligation in REQ-0020's own words, tests_the_requirement is answered false as a consequence -- the check's False paths (cmd_ack suppression, busy/dout/scl_oen/sda_oen stability) all come from Implementation Detail #2 / the ena Processing-Flow paragraph, not from this requirement's text, so the check is deciding an obligation this sentence never states. Per the briefing, this does not go back to the check's author to repair; it goes to whoever wrote the specification, since nothing the author writes can add an obligation to a sentence that has none.

REQ-0025.text: The cmd[3:0] input is the bit-level command provided by the byte-level controller.

Because there is no obligation here, the check's False path (cmd_ack completing a window with no scl_oen/sda_oen movement) cannot be a test of THIS requirement -- it is in substance the obligation stated by the routed requirements REQ-0104 and REQ-0016 (which do state that a supported cmd must drive scl_oen/sda_oen through the sequence), reused under REQ-0025's uid. This verdict is a specification issue, not a check-repair issue: no rewrite of the check can add an obligation this sentence does not state.
